title: The Fewest Guards for a Network

concept.title: Take a vertex that nobody watches: one of its neighbours (or itself) must be a guard
body: A *dominating set* of a graph is a set of vertices such that every vertex is **in the set or next to a vertex of the set** (a guard watches itself and its neighbours). We want the smallest one. For each vertex keep the bit mask `closed[v]` of the vertex and its neighbours; guarding `u` watches all vertices in `closed[u]`.

Ask "is there a dominating set of size at most `k`?" for `k = 0, 1, 2, ...` (iterative deepening). To answer, take any vertex `v` that is **not yet watched**: some guard in `closed[v]` must be chosen, so try each of them as the next guard. The search is as deep as `k` and as wide as the size of `closed[v]`, much less than the `C(n, k)` subsets.

The test with `biggest` (the largest size of a closed neighbourhood) is a **bound**: each new guard watches at most `biggest` new vertices, so at least `ceil(unwatched / biggest)` more guards are needed. When that does not fit in the remaining budget, the branch is cut at once.

statement: A graph has `n` vertices and `m` edges. A set of vertices is *dominating* if every vertex of the graph is either in the set or adjacent to a vertex of the set. Print the size of the smallest dominating set.
inputFormat: Each of the next `m` lines has two vertices joined by an edge.
constraints: 0 <= m <= n * (n - 1) / 2, no repeated edges and no loops

examples.note: The vertices 2 and 4 watch everything: the path of five vertices has a dominating set of size 2.

hints: For each vertex store a bit mask of the vertex and its neighbours.
Try the sizes k = 0, 1, 2, ... one after the other.
Pick an unwatched vertex; one of the vertices that can watch it must be chosen.

explanation: For k = 0, 1, 2, ... the search takes the lowest unwatched vertex and tries each vertex that could watch it as the next guard, stopping a branch when the number of guards still needed (unwatched vertices divided by the largest closed neighbourhood) exceeds the budget.
solution.complexity: Time exponential in k and the degrees, small for n <= 20; space O(k).
